meta.title: Macview — a light macOS image viewer that shows the picture and nothing else
meta.description: Open a picture and the picture is all you get. No buttons, no browser, just the arrow keys to move through the folder. A free and open source image viewer for macOS.

hero.title: Open a picture, and that is all you see
hero.tagline: No buttons, no browser. The window opens at the size of the picture, and the arrow keys take you to the next one in the folder. Measured here, a window is on screen about half a second after launch.
hero.note: Free and open source. For Apple silicon Macs running macOS 14 Sonoma or later.
hero.firstRun: The first launch has to be opened from the right-click menu

items.title: Nothing on screen but the picture
items.body: No toolbar, no sidebar, no title bar. The picture sits on a plain dark ground, so its colours and detail are what you are looking at.

items.title: Whatever your Mac can read, it opens
items.body: JPEG, PNG, HEIC, WebP, AVIF, GIF, TIFF and the camera RAW formats. The reading is left to macOS itself, so there are no plug-ins to add.

items.title: Quick to open, quick to be rid of
items.body: About half a second from launch to a window. The app is 1.6 MB, it does not sit in the background, and Escape closes it.

items.title: Animations play as they were made
items.body: Animated GIF, APNG and animated WebP play at the speed written in the file.

keys.title: Keys
keys.note: Scrolling and pinching zoom as well. While the picture is larger than the window, dragging moves the picture; while it is not, dragging moves the window. A double-click fills the screen, and a second one puts it back. Files can also be dropped on the window.

screens.window: The window opens at the size of the picture

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Macview is an app for looking at pictures. It collects nothing. There is little to write here, so this is short.

sections.title: It does not go on the network
sections.body: Macview makes no connections. It does not even check for updates, so nothing leaves your Mac when you launch it or open a picture. There is no server behind it and no account.

sections.title: Pictures are only opened
sections.body: A picture you open is read in order to put it on screen. Nothing is sent anywhere, nothing is copied, nothing is recorded. The app has no way to write at all.

sections.title: There is no analytics
sections.body: No crash reporting, no usage measurement, no device identifier, no third-party SDK is in the app.

sections.title: You can check
sections.body: Macview is published under the MIT license. None of this has to be taken on trust: read the source, and open an issue if something looks wrong.

sections.title: About this site
sections.body: This page is hosted on Vercel and counts page views with Vercel Web Analytics. No value identifying a person is stored. It has nothing to do with the app.
